Q: How to declare functions in a header file that are defined in a DLL A:

@XJDHDR "The question is about how to declare DLL functions, not how to figure out what a function does." You can't declare the function if you don't know what its original signature was when the DLL was compiled. If you need to reverse engineer that knowledge, knock yourself out. You will have to do it by hand, there are no tools to do it 100% automatically for you. But tools like IDA can get you close. If the functions have simple signatures, it should not take you very long to figure it out. But if the signatures are more complex then it's going to take a lot more work to figure things out.

Q: Use data pack in spigot plugin A:

You can't "import" a Data Pack into a plugin JAR. Instead, your plugin must act as a trigger for the Data Pack's logic.

  1. Identify the Trigger: Check the Data Pack's functions folder for the starting command (usually a /tag or a /function).
  2. Trigger via API:
  • Using Tags: entity.addScoreboardTag("Tag");
  • Using Commands: Bukkit.dispatchCommand(Bukkit.getConsoleSender(), "execute as " + uuid + " run function namespace:animate");
  1. Note for 1.21.1: Data Packs are world-specific. Ensure the pack is located in the /datapacks folder of the world where the animation should play.

Q: DDD Aggregate Roots: How to avoid loading unused child entities without tightly coupling to the ORM? A:

Thank you for sharing your valuable insights! I really appreciate it, as it's hard to find in-depth discussions about practical DDD out there. I have a follow-up question regarding your point:

You are allowed to have different domain models for different use cases, even when these models overlap in the persistance layer. This is called a polysemic domain model.

Wouldn't this approach lead to a lot of code duplication across different domain models? For example, let's say we have an Order in the database. Use Case A (Shipping) might need an Order model focusing on ShippingAddress and Weight, while Use Case B (Invoicing) needs another Order model focusing on TotalAmount and PaymentStatus.

Wouldn't we end up maintaining multiple Order classes that share a lot of the exact same base properties (like OrderId, CreatedAt, CustomerId). Wouldn't it be really hard to maintain these duplicate models?

Q: Openclaw Ai Agent A:

For example. with a few days,I give the agent access to:

  1. a phone (WhatsApp /telegram)

  2. Google Calendars (availability per property)

  3. property data (pricing, rules, photos, etc.)

With that setup, the agent can:

  1. respond to rental inquiries like a human

  2. check availability in real time

  3. calculate pricing

  4. request booking details

  5. handle deposits

  6. confirm reservations

  7. and update calendars automatically

So far so good

Q: R - Sort individual rows of a data.table by ascending order of the value in each column A:

@jared_mamrot, yes, that works perfectly! Thank you so much!

See below:

data <- structure(list(V1 = c(20, 2, 7, 20, 48, 12), V2 = c(1, 48, 23,
    56, 28, 11), V3 = c(54, 20, 4, 51, 55, 30), V4 = c(5, 28, 6,
    6, 52, 42), V5 = c(55, 6, 55, 22, 38, 10), V6 = c(33, 3, 40,
    3, 15, 33)), row.names = c(NA, -6L), class = c("data.table",
    "data.frame"))

data.table::as.data.table(t(apply(t(data), 2, sort)))

#      V1    V2    V3    V4    V5    V6
#   <num> <num> <num> <num> <num> <num>
# 1:     1     5    20    33    54    55
# 2:     2     3     6    20    28    48
# 3:     4     6     7    23    40    55
# 4:     3     6    20    22    51    56
# 5:    15    28    38    48    52    55
# 6:    10    11    12    30    33    42
